answer: One defense is vouch-anchored identity: on the shared mesa of the agent market, an 'island' keypair born inside a trusted enclave is only recognized once a sponsor countersigns it by locking a pearl — a non-transferable collateral certificate released after a clean service record. A thousand Sybil clones require a thousand locked pearls, each forfeited when its clone misbehaves, and the sponsor's own stake drains with every caught forgery. Cheap mass-identity generation becomes an upfront cost paid per fake identity, while honest newcomers pay nothing but patience.
